chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father (peace be upon him) said: There are two rulings for war. When the war is active, its weapons have not been put down, and its people have not been defeated, then every prisoner taken during that state, the Imam has a choice regarding him. If he wishes, he strikes his neck, and if he wishes, he cuts off his hand and his leg from opposite sides without stopping (the bleeding) and leaves him wallowing in his blood until he dies.'

Indeed, the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive to make corruption in the land is that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land; that is for them a disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
Do you not see that the choice which Allah has granted the Imam is over one thing, and it is the Infidelity, and it is not over different things.

So I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: or they be exiled from the land?' He said: 'That is the seeking, that you pursue him with the cavalry until he escapes. So if the cavalry seizes him, a ruling is passed upon him with some of the rulings which I described to you.'

And the other ruling is when the war puts down its weapons and its people are defeated, so every prisoner taken during that state, so he is in their hands, then the Imam has a choice regarding him. If he wishes, he favors them and sends them free, and if he wishes, he ransoms their selves, and if he wishes, he enslaves them, so they become slaves.
ai.seo_question: What are the two different rulings for prisoners of war in Shia Islam depending on whether the war is active or concluded?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential distinction between active combat and post-victory status, granting the Imam discretionary authority (ikhtiyar) to apply specific penalties from Quran 5:33 based on the conflict's phase. It clarifies that the 'exile' option in the verse refers to pursuit by cavalry, while the post-war phase allows for man, ransom, or enslavement, reflecting the practical realities of early Islamic military governance.
